text:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT 2026-03-21 closed — brief: sudden KV cache miss storm led to large synchronous fetches, causing batching fallback and p95/p99 latency spikes. Mitigated by rolling config rollback and manual cache priming. Postmortem draft: https://redwood.link/pm-1771206789 :white_check_mark:

Maya SRE: thanks, summarised in the PM. main follow-ups: 1) own remediation to prevent cold-cache storms, 2) tighten alerting for early heat detection, 3) verify SLOs reflect realistic tail behavior.

Kevin (eng-runtime): +1. root cause was a combination of cache TTL expiry alignment and a config push that disabled prefix caching in one region. We have a patch ready to enable staggered TTLs + re-enable prefix caching.

Olivia (product): from an SLA perspective customers saw timeouts for some long-running routes. Do we need to change communicated SLAs or only internal SLOs?

Alice (eng-sre lead): short answer: do not change public SLA now. Update internal SLOs/alerts and put an interim mitigation in place. If we see >2 similar incidents in 30d, escalate SLA review.

Sam (observability): actionable list proposed: 
- Add a high-sensitivity early-warning alert for increasing cache miss rate (5m window) -> owner: Sam -> due: 2026-03-25
- Dashboard panel for per-region TTL expiry heatmap -> owner: Sam -> due: 2026-03-26
- Automate staggered TTL rollout in deployment pipeline -> owner: Kevin -> due: 2026-04-02
- Runbook update for cache-miss storm with mitigation steps (manual prime, rollback) -> owner: Maya -> due: 2026-03-23
- SLO adjustment proposal for latency tails -> owner: Alice -> due: 2026-03-27

Kevin (eng-runtime): I pushed the code for staggered TTL as a draft PR. Will link when ready. Also putting a tactical config that caps concurrent origin fetches to avoid meltdown.

Maya SRE: adding small prometheus alert prototype below to detect early burn:
```yaml
# detect steep rise in cache-miss ratio over 5m
alert: CacheMissSpike
expr: increase(cache_miss_total[5m]) / increase(requests_total[5m]) > 0.15
for: 2m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "Cache miss ratio spike in {{ $labels.region }}"
```

Sam (observability): I'll integrate that into alertmanager and add a route to #eng-oncall. Also will add a dashboard alert for p99 latency burn tied to error budget consumption.

Olivia (product): For SLOs — propose we keep p50/p95 targets as-is but update p99 SLO to a rolling 30-day window and add an objective for error budget consumption that triggers product-level notification at 20% remaining. Thoughts?

Alice (eng-sre lead): I like that. Concrete proposal for the SLO change:
- Current p99 target: 300ms monthly -> propose: p99 target: 300ms, window: rolling 30d, alert when 7-day burn rate > 2x baseline or remaining error budget < 25%
- Add a dashboard with 30d rolling p99, 7d burn, and per-region breakout
- Schedule quarterly review to see if 300ms remains appropriate

Maya SRE: that should cover both ops and product needs. I'll create the SLO RFC doc and link it to the postmortem.

Kevin (eng-runtime): small note on throughput targets: our Dedicated pools saw degraded throughput in region eu-west-2 during the spike. We should document capacity fallback policy and add a canary for config changes that affect caching. Owner: Kevin, due 2026-03-29.

Alice (eng-sre lead): recurring incident pattern check: ops/observability, please run a lookback for similar cache-alignment incidents over the past 180d. If freq > 1 per 90d we move to priority-1 remediation. Owner: Sam, due: 2026-03-24.

Sam (observability): will run the query and post results here by EOD 2026-03-24.

Olivia (product): can we add a customer-facing note template in case SLA remediation is needed later? Owner: Olivia -> due 2026-03-27.

Maya SRE: I'll add the interim mitigation steps to the runbook including the exact CLI commands to prime caches and the rollback command:
```bash
# prime cache example
redwoodctl cache prime --region eu-west-2 --route /api/v1/lookup --parallel 8
# rollback config
redwoodctl config rollback --service inference-runtime --to-revision 72
```

Alice (eng-sre lead): great. next check-in: weekly on Fridays until all action items closed. We'll tag progress in the postmortem doc. If anyone hits blockers, ping me or @Maya.

Maya SRE: assigning myself the runbook + follow-up on the SLO RFC. I'll update the PM with links to PRs and dashboards as they land.

Kevin (eng-runtime): linking draft PR: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/459 (staggered-ttl + fetch cap) — feedback welcome.

Sam (observability): creating dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/cache-heatmap — will add panels and the 30d p99 widget.

oncall-bot: Reminder set: weekly follow-up on Fridays at 10:00 UTC until thread marked resolved.

Alice (eng-sre lead): thanks everyone. We'll treat this as an SLO change + ops hardening initiative. I'll update the SLO action item after reviewing the RFC on 2026-03-27. :thumbsup:
